mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically for four consecutive weekly means (-45.6 to -36.7), and this serial momentum reflects the removal of prior mobility constraints; absent a new shock, the same weekly increment carries forward into the next 28 days, so mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means rose from -45.6 at t-3w to -36.7 at t-0w for four straight weeks
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the 28 days after 2021-09-15 is less than or equal to -41.5 (the mean of the last four weekly values).

mechanism_narrative: Transit-station use is the binding constraint on discretionary trips into commercial districts; TRANSIT improved 7.3 points in the final week (from -40.3 to -33.0), and once the weekly TRANSIT mean crosses above -35.0 the additional station entries are converted into non-commute retail-and-recreation trips within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -35.0 percent change from baseline (it printed -33.0 at t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -40.3 at t-1w to -33.0 at t-0w, a 7.3-point single-week jump
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT is above -35.0, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is at or below its level in the preceding 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The joint release of two constraints is what unlocks discretionary retail spend: GROCERY_PHARM normalizing (from -21.7 to -11.3) shows precautionary stockpiling is ending while RESIDENTIAL falling (from +11.0 to +8.7) shows fewer hours spent at home. Only when both move together does the substitution from home-provisioning and home-based leisure into out-of-home retail-and-recreation occur.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 5 points and RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point over the same two-week window
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 10.4 points and RESIDENTIAL fell 2.3 points across the four weeks ending 2021-09-15
failure_condition: When both GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 5 points and RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days still averages lower than the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Tightened indoor-venue health-verification requirements raise the perceived cost of entering gyms, restaurants and entertainment venues, suppressing discretionary in-person visits faster than grocery or pharmacy trips are affected; the resulting indoor-venue attrition pulls RETAIL_REC down within one week of enforcement.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC remained 36.7 points below baseline at t-0w, leaving large scope for mandate-induced further attrition
regime_hint: tightening indoor-venue health mandates (venue entry verification enforced from mid-September 2021)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the 7 days after 2021-09-15 is equal to or higher than its value in the 7 days before, with no widening of the RETAIL_REC minus GROCERY_PHARM gap.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS crossing from -14.9 to +0.7 marks the tail of the summer outdoor-activity regime, and outdoor trips in this metro are chained with adjacent errands and eat-in stops; the positive PARKS level therefore keeps discretionary trip volume elevated, supporting RETAIL_REC for the two weeks before cool-weather decay sets in.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean is above 0.0 percent change from baseline (printed +0.7 at t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -14.9 at t-3w to +0.7 at t-0w, a 15.6-point swing
failure_condition: In the 7 days after 2021-09-15, RETAIL_REC falls while PARKS remains at or above 0.0, showing the two series are uncoupled.

mechanism_narrative: Weekday office presence and transit use are complements for midtown retail-and-recreation footfall; WORKPLACES recovering from -50.9 to -44.3 combined with TRANSIT at -33.0 re-creates the commuter-and-visitor base that supports lunchtime, after-work and errand spending, so the joint move raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean rises by at least 4 points while TRANSIT weekly mean simultaneously rises (both conditions must hold)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rebounded from -50.9 at t-1w to -44.3 at t-0w and TRANSIT from -40.3 to -33.0 in the same week
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES rises by at least 4 points while TRANSIT also rises, mean RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days is not higher than over the preceding 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The summer-to-autumn transition removes outdoor recreation and sidewalk-adjacent consumption: RESIDENTIAL stops declining as school and cooler weather pull activity back indoors, while PARKS above-zero readings decay from their seasonal peak, draining the trip-chaining volume that has been lifting retail-and-recreation mobility.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stops declining (week-on-week change of 0.0 or above) while PARKS weekly mean falls back below 0.0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL decelerated from a 1.0-point weekly drop (t-3w to t-2w) to a 0.9-point drop (t-1w to t-0w)
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the 28 days after 2021-09-15 is higher than over the prior 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL flattening and PARKS dropping below 0.0.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remaining positive but falling means households are shifting time out of the home without yet abandoning home-based habits; the marginal hour released each week is spent disproportionately on nearby retail and recreation, so the next week's RETAIL_REC mean improves relative to the current one.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell in every week of the window (+11.0 to +8.7) while RETAIL_REC rose in every week
failure_condition: In the 7 days after 2021-09-15, RESIDENTIAL falls further but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its t-0w value of -36.7.
